sources.name: USGS 3DEP lidar hillshade (multidirectional)
sources.what: Bare-earth shaded relief of the United States from the 3DEP elevation mosaic; mounds, earthworks, old roads and field systems show up where 1 m lidar exists.

coverage.note: United States and territories; 1 m where lidar has been flown, coarser DEMs elsewhere

variants.name: Slope Map (grey flat, yellow gentle, red-brown steep)
Contour 25 (25 contours across the view, transparent PNG)
Raw Hillshade function with your own sun: Azimuth 90, Altitude 20, ZFactor 3

sources.notes: One image per tile from exportImage. Rendering rule names as the service lists them: Hillshade Gray, Hillshade Gray-Stretch, Hillshade Multidirectional, Hillshade Elevation Tinted, Slope Map, Slope Degrees, Aspect Map, Aspect Degrees, Contour 25, Contour Smoothed 25, Preset 2ft Contour Interval, Preset 5ft Contour Interval, Preset 10ft Contour Interval, None. Sun angle: rasterFunctionArguments on a named template are ignored (same bytes came back); use the raw function {"rasterFunction":"Hillshade","rasterFunctionArguments":{"Azimuth":90,"Altitude":20,"ZFactor":3}} instead, which worked and can be nested in Stretch. 1 m pixels are fully resolved at z17; deeper zooms are upsampled. Slow and sometimes flaky: 0.5 to 10 s per tile, and one 502 in about 40 requests today. Max image 8000 px. size=512 also works.

sources.name: USGS 3DEP raw elevation (LERC or 32-bit TIFF)
sources.what: Raw bare-earth heights in metres for any Web Mercator tile, so the globe or a script can compute its own hillshade, slope or local relief.

coverage.note: United States and territories; 1 m where lidar has been flown

variants.name: 32-bit float GeoTIFF (image/tiff, about 263 kB per 256 px tile)

sources.notes: Both forms send Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *. The LERC is version 1 (the file starts with 'CntZImage'), float32 metres, and comes back as application/octet-stream (decode with Esri's lerc.js); the TIFF is uncompressed float32 (decode with geotiff.js). Not a picture a browser can draw directly. Tested tile over Monks Mound gave heights 122.8 to 158.2 m. Same speed and reliability caveats as the hillshade entry.

sources.name: USGS 3DEP lidar point clouds (Entwine EPT on AWS)
sources.what: The full classified point clouds behind 3DEP, one EPT per project, for agents that want to grid their own terrain model or look under canopy.

coverage.note: United States; 2,283 projects in the boundaries index today

variants.name: Project footprints (GeoJSON, 8.8 MB; properties name, id, count, url)

sources.notes: Keyless, and the bucket sends CORS *. To find the project covering a point: load resources.geojson (MultiPolygon per project), point-in-polygon, then read the feature's url (its ept.json). Or ask the OpenTopography catalog (entry opentopography-catalog). EPT is in EPSG:3857; read with PDAL readers.ept and a bounds filter. The tested project IL_10CoNRCS_3_D23 (covers Cahokia) holds 199,759,450,216 points. URL pattern: https://s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com/usgs-lidar-public/<project>/ept.json; the access URL above is that example project.

sources.name: USGS 3DEP elevation and lidar coverage index
sources.what: Shows where 1 m DEMs and lidar point clouds exist in the United States, so you know whether a blank-looking hillshade is real or just coarse data.
sources.notes: Layer ids: 1 '1 meter', 2 '1/9 arc-second', 3 '5 meter (Alaska only)', 4 '1/3 arc-second', 5 '1 arc-second', 8 'Lidar Point Cloud', 13 to 16 topobathymetric indexes, 18 to 30 query copies. Layers also answer /query for the project name and dates at a point. max_zoom is a practical cap; it is a vector overlay with no native pixel size.

sources.name: USGS WESM (lidar project metadata index)
sources.what: One row per 3DEP lidar project with dates, quality level and links, for agents that need to know when and how an area was flown.
sources.notes: The GeoPackage is 3.83 GB (project polygons); the CSV is 2.27 MB. No CORS header. Keyless.

sources.name: USGS TNM Access API (product search)
sources.what: Finds downloadable USGS products (lidar LAZ tiles, 1 m DEM GeoTIFFs, historical topo maps) for a bounding box.
sources.notes: Keyless, CORS *. bbox is in degrees. The tested query (dataset 'Lidar Point Cloud (LPC)', a box over Cahokia) returned total 22 with download URLs. Parameters: datasets (exact product name), bbox=west,south,east,north, max, outputFormat=JSON.

sources.name: England: Environment Agency LIDAR Composite DTM 1 m hillshade
sources.what: Bare-earth hillshade of England at 1 m; hillforts, barrows, ridge and furrow and Roman roads are plain to see.

coverage.note: England (approximate box); gaps where no lidar was flown

variants.name: Elevation colour ramp (layer Lidar_Composite_Elevation_DTM_1m, style elevation)

sources.notes: Use the KVP form shown. The REST-style tile paths in the capabilities document point at /geoservices/... and return 400 with no CORS header. The old ArcGIS endpoint environment.data.gov.uk/image/rest/services now answers 'Invalid URL'. Tiles are served to z24 but 1 m data is resolved at z17; deeper is upsampled. A 2 m composite sits at .../lidar-composite-digital-terrain-model-dtm-2m/wmts with layer names ending _2m. Licence: the data.gov.uk page for Environment Agency lidar says Open Government Licence; the capabilities text says only 'made freely available by Defra'.

sources.name: Scotland: public sector lidar DTM (colour ramp only)
sources.what: Elevation colour ramp of the Scottish lidar phases; it shows where lidar exists but has no hillshade style, so fine earthworks do not show.

coverage.note: Scotland, patchy: each phase and project is its own layer

license.attribution: Scottish Government / JNCC Scottish Remote Sensing Portal

sources.notes: Works with CORS *, but the only styles are colour ramps (scotland:lidar-dem, scotland:lidar-dem-viridis, scotland:lidar-presence). Layers: scotland:scotland-lidar-1-dtm to -6-dtm, scotland:nlp-dtm, Historic Environment Scotland project layers (scotland:scotland-gov-lidar-hes-...), Outer Hebrides 25 cm and 50 cm, Orkney 2023, each with a -dsm twin. I did not find a licence statement on a page I could fetch (the portal is a script-only app), so share_ok is false until someone reads the portal's terms. max_zoom is the deepest zoom I tested, not a measured limit.

The only lidar layers are tile catalogues: geonode:welsh_government_lidar_tile_catalogue_2020_2023, geonode:nrw_lidar_tile_catalogue_archive, inspire-nrw:NRW_LIDAR_ARCHIVE_TILE_CATALOGUE. The lidar viewer draws its hillshades from somewhere else that I did not trace. Licence not confirmed on a fetched page.

Transport Infrastructure Ireland, 2 m DTM hillshade

sources.name: Netherlands: AHN4 0.5 m DTM hillshade (Esri Nederland)

license.name: Esri Nederland Terms of Use (data itself: AHN, CC0)

sources.what: Lidar terrain shading for all of Sweden; shows ancient field systems, grave fields and charcoal pits in forest.

It is the map service behind Lantmäteriet's own 'Min karta' web app, not a documented public API, so it may change or be closed without notice. Lantmäteriet's open data is CC0, but I did not confirm that this view service is covered, so share_ok is false. I tested z15 only, so max_zoom is a floor, not a limit. Tested near Gamla Uppsala.

sources.name: Estonia: Maa-amet relief shading (national grid only)
